subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The interval from C up to G is a:
questions.explain: C up to G spans five letter names, making a perfect 5th.

questions.q: A perfect cadence is formed by which chord progression?
questions.explain: A perfect cadence moves from chord V to chord I, sounding finished.

questions.q: Repeating a short melodic pattern at higher or lower pitches in turn is called a:
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic idea at successively higher or lower pitches.

questions.q: What does a natural sign do?
options: Cancels a previous sharp or flat
Raises a note by a tone
Lowers a note by a tone
questions.explain: A natural cancels a sharp or flat, returning the note to its natural pitch.

questions.q: A plagal cadence (often called the 'Amen' cadence) is:
questions.explain: A plagal cadence moves from chord IV to chord I.

questions.q: Which cadence ends on chord V, sounding unfinished?
questions.explain: An imperfect cadence ends on chord V and sounds incomplete.

questions.q: A minim is worth how many crotchet beats?
questions.explain: A minim is worth two crotchet beats.

questions.q: Two quavers together are worth the same as one:
questions.explain: Two quavers equal one crotchet beat.

options: Composing music to meet a given set of requirements or purpose
questions.explain: Composing to a brief means writing music that fulfils a specified purpose or set of instructions.

questions.q: A major triad is built from which intervals above the root?
questions.explain: A major triad stacks a major 3rd then a minor 3rd, giving a bright sound.

questions.q: How many beats does a crotchet last in 4/4 time?
questions.explain: A crotchet lasts one beat in 4/4 time.

questions.q: A DAW used for recording and sequencing music stands for:
questions.explain: DAW means Digital Audio Workstation, software used to record, edit and sequence music.
